correctness.rationale: For normalized area on \(S_p\), each \(F_p^j\) horizontal hit has probability \(p\); a union bound gives \(\Pr(a\le N)\le Np\), and thus \(\mathbb E\log(pa)\ge-1\). The mean induced return length is \((2-p)/p\) by conditional Kac recurrence. The matrices \(M_{a,b}\) preserve the cone \(K_p=\{v\ge u/p\}\), with one-return expansion at least \(ab/[p^2(1+p)]\) and at least \(L(p)=1+p^{-2}+(1+p)^{-1}\). Jensen bounds the induced upper growth by \(2\log(1+p^{-2})\). After return-time normalization, the explicit inequalities squeeze the sharp coefficient \(2\). Exact-rational checks confirm finite samples but are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The sharp small-width scaling is not a consequence of the range-limited explicit theorem in Wright–Niesen–Sturman (2023), nor of fixed-parameter correlation-decay theorems in Springham–Sturman (2014). A previously uncombined uniform short-return tail estimate supplies logarithmic moments sufficient to squeeze the exact coefficient. Three closest semantic records have different systems/statements; bounded priority risk is recorded.

value.rationale: The canonical equal-strip linked-twist family models shear-induced chaotic mixing, and the overlap-width limit \(p\downarrow0\) is a singular regime outside the range of the principal published explicit Lyapunov bounds. The law \(2p\log(1/p)+O(p)\) quantifies the decay of instability beyond fixed-width positivity, and a width-uniform short-return argument bypasses an otherwise complicated thin-strip return partition. This precise scaling is useful in comparing weakly overlapping shear-flow channels.
